systems.tiers: BEAC, two Treasuries, banks, microfinance institutions, payment institutions and mobile money operators, aggregators

note: Reports GIMACPAY activity and 16 payment institutions and mobile money operators among participants; names no law or rule on licensing or connection, and participation is not stated as required.

facts.fact: COBAC's 2025 annual report, as relayed by Ecomatin, counts seven licensed payment institutions (etablissements de paiement) in CEMAC in 2025, of which Orange Money Cameroun and Mobile Money Corporation SA (MTN) operate in Cameroon; the source names no law or regulation by title.

Konoom Cameroun was licensed as a payment institution (etablissement de paiement) by arrete n°681/MINFI of 21 July 2026, following COBAC decision n°D-2026/092; Orange Money Cameroun and Mobile Money Corporation (MTN) were already licensed, per DGTCFM data of July 2026; the source names no law by title.

Agence Ecofin states that Cameroon's regulatory framework lets payment institutions and also banks and microfinance institutions offer payment services under the conditions the regulation sets; published 2026-09-17, the source gives no date for the framework and names no law by title.

The document gives only the Findex account-ownership share (60.87% in 2024); it states nothing on this question.

facts.fact: CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC Regulation 04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services imposes opposition and blocking means, a permanent complaints mechanism and transaction authenticity solutions, and mobile money falls under it.

note: The article covers a World Bank G2Px awareness workshop on salary and pension payments; it states nothing on the payment topics asked.

facts.fact: The Prime Minister's order of 28 May 2025 cites CEMAC regulation 03/16/CEMAC/UMAC/CM of 21 December 2016 on payment systems and incidents as a legal basis, alongside a finance ministry order of 28 February 2024 on approving electronic payment service providers.
